messages:
maria: quick update — ran a regional switchover smoke run against the replay harness for kernel-selection changes. saw a 95th latency bump (~220ms -> ~520ms) for short sequences after route switch. sketch below.

raj: ugh that's bigger than i hoped. do you have the profiler traces?

maria: pasted a small snippet from the runtime profiler (trimmed):
```
kv_cache_metrics: hit_rate=0.72
kernel_choice: default->compact16 at step t=0 (after routing change)
batch_size_hist: pre=8 median, post=1 median
latency_p95_ms: 220 -> 520
```

eli: interesting — batch collapse to 1 median points to bursty routing decisions. could be our scheduling window + switch causing debatching.

sophia: +1. also see KV cache cold-start when the request set moves region. 0.72 hit rate is okay, but effective miss penalty with compact kernel is higher.

maria: i reproduced with a like-for-like replay (same client IDs, same arrival shape). when routing flips to the secondary region, the model variant mapping returns a compact-quantized kernel for cost reasons; that kernel has a higher per-token tail for short sequences under low-batch.

raj: so two levers: (1) routing policy that avoids moving to cheaper-but-s lower-throughput kernels mid-flight, (2) batching heuristic to keep minimum batch window during switchover.

eli: can we try a conservative kernel-pin for 60s after any region switch? keep the previous kernel selection until the KV cache primes.

maria: ran that as a quick patch — added a sticky kernel TTL of 45s after route-change. result: p95 drops to ~270ms in same test. not ideal but way better.

sophia: nice. what's the cost delta? are we pinning a heavier kernel?

maria: cost up ~4% for that window. we should quantify across steady-state traffic.

raj: also try bumping minimum batching window from 2ms to 8ms for the switchover period. Might trade a few ms median for much lower p95.

maria: tested 8ms min-window + sticky kernel: p50 unchanged, p95 ~240ms. response tail much tighter.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-05-09T15:20:45Z by mariaruntime — canary routing-pin + sticky-kernel feature flags enabled on test env

maria: note: KV cache priming looked noisy — for some user cohorts the cache warm-up was ~20s, others ~6s. hypothesis: arrival-parallelism matters (many small concurrent sessions prime better).

eli: idea: pre-warm KV for critical prefixes when signaling a planned region switch (control-plane signal). will need to measure bandwidth + memory impact.

sophia: agree. Also add monitoring: per-route kernel-switch counters, batching-window distribution, and kv-miss latency percentiles. add an alert if p95 increases >30% after route change.

maria: opened a quick ticket with traces + dashboards: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/rt/1765567899 — includes flamegraphs and the like-for-like run.

raj: action items:
- run full sweep of client arrival shapes (burst, steady, poisson) with sticky-kernel/8ms window (eli)
- evaluate cost impact over 24h traffic (sophia)
- prototype pre-warm signal and simulate network/kv load (maria)
- add observability + alert (raj)

eli: will run the sweep today. starting with synthetic flood -> ramp -> steady. will report numbers in this thread.

maria: thanks. quick note: loadbot flagged an odd regression in kernel selector after last runtime merge — small PR incoming to fix threshold math.

loadbot: perf-regress-detect: candidate change in kernel-scoring v2.2 looks correlated with increased compact selection under low-batch.

sophia: ping @raj if that PR touches policy table. want to avoid churn in prod.

raj: got it, will review asap.

eli: preliminary results from synthetic sweep: with sticky+8ms -> p95 averaged 235ms across all shapes; without sticky -> 510ms for bursty arrival. I'll post raw CSV in the ticket.

maria: solid. closing loop — we'll keep sticky-kernel behind a short-lived feature flag while we measure cost/benefit and build pre-warm. smallish risk path to mitigate region switchover pain. :thumbsup:
